To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) STDP with teacher forced learning converges for uncorrelated Poisson input spike patterns, (ii) STDP with correlated Poisson input spikes converges if the cross-correlation function of the input spikes is a linear separable function, and (iii) these results also hold for the more realistic interpretation of STDP where the initial release probability is modified.
STDP with teacher-forcing converges for Poisson input spike patterns and realistic spiking neuron models if and only if the input spike trains can be linearly separated.

STDP with teacher-forcing can learn any linearly separable transformation F, but not any arbitrary transformation F, and that this result holds for biologically realistic models of spiking neurons, dynamic synapse, and correlated Poisson inputs, as well as for a more realistic version of STDP where the release probability of dynamic synaptic vesicles is modulated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether a spiking neuron can be taught to implement an arbitrary transformation of its input by STDP.
the question to what extend a neuron with biologically reasonable models for dynamic synapse and spike timing can learn with STDP to implement a given input-output transformation.
the theoretical and experimental analysis of the learning capabilities of spiking neurons and their synapses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

STDP can learn a given transformation F if the columns of the input correlation matrix are linearly separable, but that the convergence of STPD with teacher forcing is in general not guaranteed for arbitrary input spike trains.

STDP with teacher-forcing is an effective learning rule for a wide class of transformations F that are learnable by perceptrons, and that this class is not much smaller than the class of learnable functions for perceptrons.
the perceptron convergence theorems are not only applicable in the case of McCulloch-Pitt's neurons but also for spiking neurons with biologically realistic dynamic synapses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
STDP with teacher-forcing can learn any linearly separable transformation, but not more than that.

a spiking neuron is capable to learn a transformation F from uncorrelated Poisson spike input to uncorrelated Poissson output spike trains if and only if F is linearly separable in the sense of the correlation matrices of the input Poisson spike trains.
the perceptron convergence theory holds in the average case for a wide class of input spike trains and realistic models for spiking neuron models, dynamic synapses and STDP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a neuron with STDP can indeed learn a wide class of transformations from input spike trains, but only if it is given the correct target signal to learn.
a neuron can be taught with STDP to implement a transformation F if and only if F is linearly separable with respect to a certain correlation matrix of the input spike train.

a spiking neuron can indeed be taught via STDP to implement a given linearly separable transformation F, if the input distribution is sufficiently simple, e.g., uncorrelated or correlated Poisson spike trains.
